messages:
tomas: Heads-up: the SRE RBAC tweak scheduled for tomorrow might allow expanded metadata access to customer-managed keys (BYOK) for debugging. We need a quick sync on limits + audit controls before the rollout.

sara: which metadata fields? key-id only or key-usage/creation?

tomas: proposal from infra: read-only visibility to key-id, creation_ts, attached policies. No key material export. But they asked for ability to see 'attachment context' (app owner) which could leak tenant mapping.

kevin-platform: we should avoid mapping tenant -> key in any UI unless customer opted in. Platform can expose key-id and masked tenant aliases.

maria-legal: +1. From a compliance POV (SOC2 / PCI), we must justify any access that could identify customer keys. If this is a fallback for oncall, we need JIT access + approval audit trail.

lee-sre: for oncall, we often need to correlate a failing node to the key-id to validate cache/kv issues. If we can't see tenant mapping, debugging becomes painful. Is there a way to show correlation without revealing tenant identity?

kevin-platform: idea: expose hashed tenant id in logs and UI with a reversible mapping only during an authorized incident window (requires approval token). That way normal users see no mapping.

maria-legal: reversible mappings are fine only if the unmasking is gated (2 approvers) and fully audited. Need retention policy for unmask events and proof in audit logs.

audit-bot: NOTE: all unmask/unlock events must create an immutable audit record: user, approvers, reason, TTL, related incident id.

lee-sre: ok, then propose flow: (1) SRE requests unmask with incident id, (2) paged approver approves in <5m, (3) system logs event and issues short-lived token (5m) to reveal tenant alias.

tomas: we'll need changes in RBAC roles: add new permission 'kms:unmask-customer-mapping' scoped to oncall role. Default false. Documented and reviewed in access matrix.

kevin-platform: also add 'kms:list-keys-metadata' for read-only metadata; separate from 'kms:unmask-customer-mapping'. We should prevent service accounts from having unmask permission.

maria-legal: require quarterly attestation for any humans with unmask permission. Add to access review playbook.

lee-sre: what about audit log integrity? If an attacker can tamper with logs, unmask events could be hidden.

tomas: plan: forward HSM/KMS audit logs to an immutable append-only store (WORM) with retention per customer SLA, sign entries using system key, and ship a digest to external vendor for cross-checks.

kevin-platform: note: for private deployments / on-prem, customers manage their own HSMs so we cannot sign logs. We'll surface 'local-ops' audit guidelines and require customers to attest.

maria-legal: include language in contract addendum for Private deploys: we don't have custody or control over key material or local logs; customer must maintain tamper-evident logs.

lee-sre: vuln triage question: if we detect a compromised SRE account that performed unmask, what’s our response? immediate revoke tokens, rotate any session keys, start forensic snapshot?

tomas: yes: incident playbook steps: (A) revoke unmask perms and tokens, (B) collect signed audit logs and snapshots, (C) notify customer if their key mapping was revealed, (D) if key compromise suspected, coordinate with KMS team for emergency rotation options and fallback routing.

kevin-platform: add an automated watcher that flags high-volume unmask attempts or same user unmasking many tenants in short window. Trigger incident P1.

maria-legal: also ensure we have pre-approved customer notification templates and SLA for disclosure that meet regulatory timelines.

lee-sre: Dev question: CLI for JIT unmask? can we do something like:```
redwood kms unmask --key-id=abc123 --incident=INC-2026-001 --approver=ops-lead
```

kevin-platform: yes, implement as API endpoint with approval webhook. CLI will be a wrapper. Response should never include plaintext tenant id unless token active.

tomas: one more: telemetry for Optimize and logging — make sure telemetry strips any tenant-identifying fields when exported for aggregate cost analysis.

maria-legal: agreed. Need docs for customers describing exactly what metadata we store, how long, and disclosure windows.

tomas: action items: (1) kevin: prototype unmask flow + UI mock (due EOD Tues), (2) lee: draft incident runbook and detection rules (due Wed), (3) maria: contract language snippets + attestation cadence (due Fri), (4) sara: add RBAC permissions to access matrix PR and ownership.

sara: I'll open a PR against infra-access-matrix and add a short checklist for onboard.

kevin-platform: I'll add audit-bot alerts and a basic UI mock.

maria-legal: cc: legal-privacy for review once draft ready.

tomas: thanks all. I'll pause the RBAC rollout until we have the PR and basic mock. :thumbsup:

lee-sre: thanks — please ping #incidents when detection rules are live so oncall knows thresholds.

sara: pinged. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-access-matrix/pull/452

kevin-platform: mock link: https://figma.internal/redwood/file/Byo-Unmask-Flow

maria-legal: filed ticket for contract addendum:  PROJ-1442
